metadata.title: 1998 Case 31
metadata.original_presentation: An eight-year-old boy was admitted to the hospital because of a history of respiratory problems and evidence of bronchiectasis.

required.content: What is the patient's history of respiratory problems?
required.response: The boy had been well until three months before admission, when he was seen by a physician because of a cough and low-grade fever. He had a history of pneumonia with night sweats and spikes of fever two years before admission.

teaching_points.content: A history of respiratory symptoms such as cough and fever can indicate underlying pulmonary conditions.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical history?
required.response: The boy was treated for tuberculosis two years before admission, although no tubercle bacilli were detected.

teaching_points.content: A history of tuberculosis treatment can complicate the diagnosis of current respiratory issues.

required.content: What is the patient's travel and immigration history?
required.response: The boy is a native of El Salvador and immigrated to this country nine months before admission.

teaching_points.content: Travel and immigration history can provide clues to infectious diseases endemic to certain regions.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Post-tuberculosis bronchiectasis
refuting_evidence: no tubercle bacilli detected during previous treatment
additional_information_needed: chest CT scan to assess extent of bronchiectasis
sputum culture to rule out active TB

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cystic Fibrosis
refuting_evidence: no mention of gastrointestinal symptoms or failure to thrive
ethnic background less common for CF

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection
refuting_evidence: no specific mention of non-tuberculous mycobacterial exposure

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia
refuting_evidence: no mention of situs inversus or other characteristic features

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: The results of a physical examination were normal except for dullness and bronchial breathing over the right lung base and right axilla.

teaching_points.content: Dullness and bronchial breathing can indicate consolidation or atelectasis in the lung.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Post-tuberculosis bronchiectasis
supporting_evidence: dullness and bronchial breathing over the right lung base
refuting_evidence: no tubercle bacilli detected during previous treatment
additional_information_needed: chest CT scan to assess extent and location of bronchiectasis
sputum culture to rule out active infection

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Recurrent pneumonia
supporting_evidence: history of pneumonia with night sweats and fever
refuting_evidence: normal physical examination except for localized findings
additional_information_needed: chest X-ray to check for current pneumonia
complete blood count to assess for infection

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection
refuting_evidence: no current evidence of mycobacterial infection

required.content: What were the findings on imaging studies?
required.response: Chest radiographs showed densely opacified right lower and middle lobes, sharply marginated, with volume loss and areas of bronchiectasis. CT scan revealed atelectasis and bronchiectasis of the right middle and lower lobes, and a noncalcified endobronchial lesion in the bronchus intermedius.

teaching_points.content: Imaging studies are crucial for diagnosing structural lung diseases such as bronchiectasis and atelectasis.

required.content: What were the laboratory test results?
required.response: The levels of urea nitrogen, creatinine, bilirubin, albumin, electrolytes, aspartate aminotransferase, lactate dehydrogenase, and alkaline phosphatase were normal. Prothrombin and partial-thromboplastin times were normal.

teaching_points.content: Normal laboratory values can help rule out systemic causes of respiratory symptoms.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Foreign body aspiration
supporting_evidence: noncalcified endobronchial lesion in the bronchus intermedius
atelectasis and bronchiectasis of the right middle and lower lobes
refuting_evidence: no acute history of choking or aspiration event noted
additional_information_needed: bronchoscopy to directly visualize and potentially remove the foreign body

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary tuberculosis
supporting_evidence: immigration from a country with high TB prevalence
refuting_evidence: no current systemic symptoms like fever or night sweats
additional_information_needed: sputum culture and PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Bronchial obstruction due to tumor
supporting_evidence: noncalcified endobronchial lesion in the bronchus intermedius
refuting_evidence: age of the patient is less typical for primary lung tumors
additional_information_needed: further imaging studies like MRI or PET scan

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA)
refuting_evidence: lack of eosinophilia or elevated IgE levels noted in the case

required.content: What was the initial management for the patient's condition?
required.response: An antibiotic was prescribed initially, but repeated radiographs remained abnormal.

teaching_points.content: Antibiotic treatment is often the first line of management for suspected bacterial infections, but persistent symptoms may require further investigation.

final_diagnosis.name: Bronchiectasis with possible endobronchial lesion
supporting_evidence: CT findings of bronchiectasis and endobronchial lesion
